title: 📊 Daily Report: Mon Oct 26, 2026
text:
The swing book closed at $19,243.43, up $66.13 against this week's Monday base. The CORE QQQ sleeve made +$67.80 of that, while the strategy traders are down $1.67, so the strategies are slightly in deficit for the week. Since the Oct 10 merge, the book is down $777.31 (-3.88%), while Indy, the SPY buy-and-hold benchmark, is down $343.20 (-1.71%), leaving us $434.11 behind the benchmark.

Two trades went through today. Sunny bought 2 shares of FANG on a sign-imbalance setup, and CORE QQQ sold a small slice to fund that entry. CORE QQQ is $17,228, about 90% of the book, and its trend filter is on: the prior close of 704.4 is above the 200-day average of 676.1. Rota and Sunny are the only active strategy bots; Trek shows no edge, and the rest are benched.

Research's analyst note for today:
- Stocks bounced after two losing weeks: Nasdaq +0.8%, S&P 500 +0.7%, Dow +0.3%. Anthropic's IPO filing (Nasdaq ticker ANT, $16.3B first-half revenue, $80.7B loss) put the AI trade back in play, and chips led with the semis index up more than 3% midday.
- Our chip and AI-capex avoids expired today, right as the group rallied. TSLA jumped about 6% on a Barclays upgrade and INTC about 6% on a Buy upgrade ahead of Thursday's earnings.
- Oil eased (WTI down about 2% to roughly $101) as regional officials flew to Tehran, which is a headwind for our energy and defense holds (SLB, HAL, XLE, LMT, RTX).
- Our VZ idea had a muted day: subscriber adds were strong, but SpaceX's coming Starlink Mobile service kept the stock around $44. The telco avoid on T and TMUS stays on.
- Next up: durable goods and consumer confidence Tuesday plus V and HOOD after the close, then the Fed decision with MSFT and GOOGL Wednesday, and GDP, PCE inflation and AMZN Thursday.
